market_sizing.target_buyer: Founder + head of operations / supply-chain lead. Often a sustainability-credentialed founder (ex-design, ex-consultant). For mid-size brands a dedicated COO.
market_sizing.business_count_au: Narrow segment — approx. 30-80 AU brands operating an explicit refill / closed-loop / reusable-packaging model at SMB scale. Leaders: Zero Co, Skipper, Thankyou, Single Use Ain't Sexy, Resparkle, Ethique (NZ), Dirt Company, Who Gives A Crap (adjacent — paper, not refill). Long tail of micro indie refill brands sold via Biome / Source Bulk Foods / Flora & Fauna. [uncertain]
market_sizing.business_count_secondary: US: ~200-400 (Blueland, Plaine Products, Grove Collaborative, Branch Basics, etc.). UK: ~100-200 (Smol, Splosh, Ecover refill). NZ: ~20-40. CA: ~50-100. [uncertain]
market_sizing.typical_size: 5-30 employees, AU$500K-AU$15M annual revenue. The segment skews larger than other Tier-A segments because refill economics require scale.
market_sizing.annual_revenue_band_aud: 1M-5M most common. Zero Co outlier at AU$20M+. Long tail at 100K-500K.
market_sizing.growth_trend: Global zero-waste refill packaging USD 2.6B -> USD 8.5B by 2035 (12.6% CAGR, Future Market Insights). Reusable & refillable packaging USD 28.2B -> USD 35.4B by 2029 (+4.6% CAGR). AU 2025 national packaging targets create regulatory tailwind (all packaging recyclable/compostable/reusable by 2025 — APCO). High-growth but small.

fit_and_timing.manuva_fit_score: 4 — strong on BOM + lot tracking + multi-location, but Manuva does NOT natively model reverse-logistics returns flow (used containers coming back, refurb, refill). Workarounds via location transfers + adjusted-receipts are clunky.
fit_and_timing.roadmap_dependency: Functional today but a true reverse-logistics module would 2x fit. Xero integration improves close rate. WooCommerce (~10% on WordPress, e.g. eco-niche). Subscription billing integration (Recharge, Bold) is important and probably already covered via Shopify.
fit_and_timing.typical_tier: Growth (AU$249) for AU$1-3M brands; Pro (AU$499) for AU$3M+ brands with multi-location.
fit_and_timing.regulatory_burden: 2 — APCO reporting + product-stewardship obligations for some categories. Not as heavy as TGA/FSANZ. Personal-care refill brands inherit AICIS overhead (overlaps with item 01).
fit_and_timing.lot_batch_criticality: 3 — depends on category: cleaning products = low, personal care = medium-high (AICIS), food refill (e.g. Source Bulk) = high.

economics.incumbent_pricing: Cin7 Core AU$349-549/mo (most mid-size sustainable brands use Cin7 or Unleashed). Unleashed NZ$319-399/mo. Katana US$199-399/mo. NetSuite at top end (Zero Co likely on NetSuite or custom). Spreadsheets rare here — these brands have ops headcount.
economics.willingness_to_pay_aud: AU$249-499/mo solid. Sustainability brands willing to pay for tools that align with their values (lower waste = lower SKU churn = better forecasting). Procurement-led — sceptical of small vendors.
economics.expansion_revenue_potential: 3 — moderate. Pro tier upgrade likely once brand hits AU$3M. Add-on appetite for capacity-planning module high.
economics.churn_risk: 2 — well-funded brands churn less. PR-sensitive — bad onboarding = public LinkedIn complaint. Reverse-logistics workflow gaps could drive churn.
economics.cac_estimate_aud: Cash CAC AU$300-700 (LinkedIn outbound + B Corp newsletter + sustainability newsletter sponsorships + 1-2 conference attendances). Founder-time CAC: ~10-15 hrs per close x AU$100/hr = AU$1,000-1,500. Longer sales cycle (2-3 months).
economics.ltv_estimate_aud: AU$350 ARPU x 36mo x 80% GM = AU$10,080.
economics.typical_seat_count: 5-15 (ops + warehouse + procurement + marketing). Per-seat MRP painful — clear flat-pricing wedge.
economics.multi_channel_count: 3-4 (Shopify + Amazon + select retail like Biome / Flora & Fauna / Coles + wholesale).
economics.wholesale_b2b_mix: 30-50% wholesale (eco-retailers, B-Corp-aligned grocers, hospitality). D2C subscription is the growth engine.

outreach_fit.cold_outbound_feasibility: 3 — LinkedIn outbound feasible but slow; founders often busy / press-hounded. B Corp community is warmer than cold. Cold email moderate (high domain authority on filtering). Best path: warm intros via B Corp ANZ Slack.
outreach_fit.inbound_content_fit: 4 — 'how to track reverse-logistics in Shopify', 'APCO reporting for SMB brands', 'circular ops case study' content converts. Long-form SEO + LinkedIn thought leadership work.
outreach_fit.founder_market_fit_proxy: 3 — sustainability founders are values-aligned buyers. Manuva must not greenwash but doesn't need sustainability credentials per se — operational competence + 'we get circular' framing suffices. Solo-founder narrative resonates ('built by a maker for makers').
outreach_fit.case_study_acquisition_cost: Medium-high — sustainability brands are PR-savvy but want polished case studies; 8-12 weeks per case study. Worth it: each case study unlocks B Corp network referrals.

foot_in_door_fit.design_partner_appeal: 4 — strong. Sustainability founders love being early adopters and shaping tools. 'Help us build the first MRP for refill brands' framing converts.
foot_in_door_fit.paid_pilot_fit: 4 — viable. AU$249 x 3 months credit-on-conversion fits AU$1M+ brands. Procurement-friendly.
foot_in_door_fit.free_trial_extension_fit: 2 — free-for-X-months feels misaligned with these brands' premium positioning. They expect to pay for quality tools.
foot_in_door_fit.trial_to_paid_benchmark: Estimated 30-40% CC-required trial -> paid (above ChartMogul baseline due to high WTP + clear ROI). Paid pilot 50-60%.
foot_in_door_fit.recommended_foot_in_door_motion: Founder-led + warm-intro motion via B Corp ANZ network. Open with 1-2 design-partner offers to recognisable mid-size refill brands (free 6mo + roadmap input on reverse-logistics module + co-built case study). Then shift to paid pilot AU$249/mo x 3 months. Sponsor 1 Naturally Good Expo + 1 B Corp event in year 1. Long-form 'circular operations' content as inbound engine.
foot_in_door_fit.rollout_phase: Phase 2 (months 3-6) — segment is small (~30-80 AU brands), so first push case studies via Phase-1 verticals (cosmetics, homewares) before approaching this premium cohort. Targeting after 3-5 Phase-1 case studies are live increases credibility.

competitive_context.current_dominant_tool: Fragmented. Cin7 Core ~25%, Unleashed ~15%, NetSuite at top end ~10%, Katana ~10%, custom/internal tools ~15%, spreadsheets ~25%. No dominant solution for the refill-specific workflow — that's the wedge.
competitive_context.competitor_gaps_for_this_segment: All incumbents lack: reverse-logistics flow (empties returning + cleaning + refill), refill-vs-new SKU pairing, APCO reporting hooks, B-Corp-friendly impact metrics. Cin7 post-acquisition pricing complaints. Manuva closes: multi-level BOMs (refill formulation + container BOM separately), location-based inventory (empties-in-transit, empties-at-cleaner, refilled-ready-to-ship), lot tracking (cleaning compliance for personal care), Shopify subscription depth.
competitive_context.user_satisfaction_signals: LinkedIn posts from refill-brand ops leads: 'we built our own reverse-logistics tracker in Airtable because nothing fits'; 'Cin7 forces us to treat empties as a separate SKU which breaks reporting'. Reddit r/sustainability + r/smallbusiness threads echo this.
competitive_context.integration_dependency_list: Must: Shopify subscription apps (Recharge, Bold, Loop), Xero (roadmap). Important: APCO reporting export, Klaviyo, Australia Post returns label API, 3PL APIs (eStore, Shippit). Nice: Faire, Amazon.

partner_channels.xero_myob_partner_channel_fit: 3 — mid-size sustainability brands use Xero or QuickBooks. ProAdvisor referrals work post-integration.
partner_channels.shopify_plus_partner_potential: 4 — many refill brands are Shopify Plus (Zero Co, Thankyou, Who Gives A Crap). Tech Partner program valuable.
partner_channels.tpl_3pl_referral_potential: 4 — strong. AU 3PLs handling refill brands (eStore Logistics, Pack & Send) are co-sell candidates. Cleaning-partner / refill-fulfilment specialists rarer.
partner_channels.industry_association_sponsorship: B Corp ANZ (member events / Slack visibility ~AU$1-3K [uncertain]). APCO membership (AU$1-5K depending on category [uncertain]). Sustainable Business Australia. Naturally Good Expo sponsor ~AU$10-25K [uncertain].

profitability_math.realistic_12mo_customer_count_solo: 5-10 paying customers in 12 months. Smaller segment, longer sales cycle (2-3 months), higher per-customer effort.
profitability_math.realistic_12mo_mrr_contribution_aud: AU$1,800-3,500 MRR at month 12 (6-8 customers x AU$350).
profitability_math.path_to_first_3k_5k_mrr_aud: Cannot hit AU$3-5K MRR on this segment alone in 12 months. Sequence: (1) months 3-4: get warm intros via 1-2 advisor relationships in B Corp ANZ (cold-start risk = high without warmth); (2) months 4-6: land 2 design partners (one personal-care refill, one cleaning/home refill); (3) months 6-9: publish reverse-logistics case study + 'circular ops cookbook' content; (4) months 9-12: convert 4-6 paid customers. Treat as supplementary revenue + high-PR-value logos that boost credibility for Phase-3 multi-channel segment.
profitability_math.customers_needed_for_1m_arr_aud: ~280 customers at AU$350 ARPU — exceeds the entire AU addressable pool. In aspirational AU$1M ARR mix, this segment contributes ~30-50 customers (~AU$130-180K ARR) as a high-prestige reference tier, not volume.
profitability_math.solo_founder_bandwidth_fit: 3 — high-touch onboarding for refill workflow (currently mapped via location-transfers — clunky). Each customer eats 8-12 founder hours initially. Manageable at 10 customers; constraining at 20+.
profitability_math.break_even_contribution_months: 3-5 months on cash CAC; 5-8 months fully loaded.
profitability_math.gross_margin_sensitivity: Moderate-high — reverse-logistics edge cases require custom support and likely build-on-demand features. Until a proper reverse-logistics module ships, GM erodes to ~70-75%.
profitability_math.priority_ranking: 4 — high-prestige but low-volume, narrow ICP, and Manuva isn't perfectly fit for the unique reverse-logistics workflow. Pursue selectively for case-study leverage, not as a volume play. Lower priority than cosmetics, SPF, pet, ceramics.
profitability_math.risks_and_notes: Risks: (1) reverse-logistics gap in Manuva means buyer disappointment risk — must be explicit in sales conversations; (2) segment is small enough that 5-10 logos = market saturation; (3) B Corp brands are PR-active — one bad story damages broader brand. Things to verify: actual count of AU refill/closed-loop brands at >AU$500K revenue; whether top brands (Zero Co, Thankyou) are on NetSuite (unreachable) or salvageable; whether a true reverse-logistics module is roadmap-worthy or whether workarounds suffice.
